title: ED arrests two accused in Kerala Cluster Case involving fake Chinese loan app scam
text: ED Kochi reported arrests of Sayid Muhammad and Varghese T G in the fake Chinese loan-app scam. It said the suspects arranged about 500 mule bank accounts with ₹719 crore in credits and 26 WazirX-linked crypto accounts, enabling ₹115.67 crore in cross-border crypto remittances to foreign wallets. ED also said part of the proceeds was remitted to Singapore through normal banking channels and Nium India against purported software or digital-goods/services imports. The release said more than 10 locations in Mumbai, Chennai and Kochi were searched in February 2024, with electronic devices seized and ₹123.58 crore frozen. Four other Tamil Nadu-linked persons had been arrested on 30 January 2025.
quoted_excerpt: ED investigation revealed that ... approx. 500 mule bank accounts ... witnessing total credit of Rs. 719 Crore.

title: Kerala Cluster Case - arrests of four accused
text: ED reported arrests of Daniel Selvakumar, Allen Samuel, Anto Paul Prakash and Kathiravan Ravi. The release linked them to Xoduz Solutions, Tyrannus Technology, Aprikiwi Solutions, Global Expositions and Infomedia Solutions, Sozo Technology and Future Vision Media Solutions. ED said more than 400 mule accounts were used to integrate ₹230.92 crore and that proceeds were routed through shell entities before being remitted to Singapore, including through Nium India. It separately reported ₹123.58 crore frozen during searches and described ₹1,677 crore as having moved through the Nium India channel, while alleging reporting-compliance lapses.
quoted_excerpt: Daniel Selvakumar, Director of M/s Xoduz Solutions Pvt. Ltd. and operator of M/s Tyrannus Technology Pvt. Ltd.

title: Sayid Muhammed vs Directorate of Enforcement, B.A. No. 7278/25
text: The Kerala High Court judgment in Sayid Muhammed's bail matter records prosecution allegations that loan apps were circulated on social media and contacted prospective users through WhatsApp, then accessed mobile-phone data for extortion. The judgment records an allegation that Sayid approached Nitin Varghese to arrange 154 bank accounts and separately managed another 290 accounts, forwarding details to Leema. It further records prosecution material alleging that account details were supplied through Leema and Angel, that Sayid arranged WazirX crypto accounts, and that ₹3.47 crore was remitted to four foreign crypto wallets. The judgment also records an allegation that ₹121 crore collected from victims was traced to four foreign wallets and that Sayid received ₹2 crore, of which ₹30 lakh was distributed to persons who arranged accounts. The bail application was dismissed.
quoted_excerpt: various Chinese loan applications were circulated on social media platforms

title: Kerala duo helped launder Rs 718 crore through mule bank accounts for Chinese loan app scam
text: The New Indian Express reported that Sayid Muhammed M M and Varghese T G were alleged to have arranged 479 mule bank accounts, with separate reporting that Sayid was associated with 289 accounts and ₹377 crore in transactions while Varghese was associated with 190 accounts and ₹341 crore. The report said account-holder details, ATM-card details and PIN information were sent to Leema and Angel via WhatsApp. It also reported WazirX-linked movement of USDT into ether and transfer to four foreign wallets, and named Xoduz Solutions, Vicky Venkat Technology and Vikrah Trading Enterprise in the company layer. The report used the spelling Daniel Shivakumar for a person identified elsewhere by ED as Daniel Selvakumar.
quoted_excerpt: Sayid arranged 289 mule bank accounts for Chinese online loan operators

title: ED arrests four Tamil Nadu natives linked to Chinese bogus loan apps
text: The New Indian Express reported on the arrests of four Tamil Nadu-linked persons and described Chinese loan apps distributed in APK form through social media. It also named Raphael James Rozario in connection with mule-bank-account arrangements and mentioned Nitin Varghese and Afreed K Y in the account-supply context. The report described account details and ATM/PIN information being passed to a woman named Leena.
quoted_excerpt: Chinese loan apps in APK format are being circulated on social media platforms

title: Chinese-controlled betting, loan apps: ED freezes bank deposits
text: India Today reported ED searches involving entities and directors connected with Chinese-controlled betting and loan-app investigations. The report said electronic devices, documents and bank accounts were examined and that Xoduz Solutions, Vikrah Trading and other entities were among those linked to the investigation.
